channel.title: Chrysler recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica may lose electronic stability control
item.description: A small electrical part inside the brake pedal sensor on these Chrysler minivans may be cracked. That sensor tells the stability control system when you are braking, and a cracked part can shut the system down. Stability control is what quietly steps in to keep the van from sliding or spinning on a wet road or in a sudden swerve. Without it, the van is harder to keep under control. A dealer will inspect the sensor and replace it if needed.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica plug-in hybrid battery can catch fire
item.description: The battery pack in these plug-in hybrid minivans can start a fire. It can happen even when the van is parked and switched off. Chrysler tells owners to stop charging the vehicle entirely and to park it outside, away from your house, garage or any other building, until it is fixed. A dealer will update the software that controls the battery pack and, if an inspection shows a problem, replace the pack itself. There is no charge for any of this.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager front airbags may not deploy
item.description: Inside the plug that connects the front seat wiring, a small spring can touch electrical contacts it is not supposed to touch. That accidental connection can stop the front airbags from going off in a crash. Nothing will feel wrong while you drive — the problem only shows up at the moment you need the airbag to protect you. These are Pacifica and Voyager vans modified by Braun Corporation. The dealer replaces the spring free of charge.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica: backup camera image may not appear
item.description: When you shift into reverse, the picture from the backup camera may not show up on the dashboard screen. This happens because of contamination inside the unit that processes the camera image, or because that unit was programmed wrong. Without that picture you cannot see people or objects directly behind the vehicle while backing up. The dealer will update the unit's software, or replace the unit if needed, free of charge.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica wheelchair restraints may not lock properly
item.description: These are Pacifica vans converted by Braun to carry a passenger in a wheelchair. The retractors — the devices that strap the wheelchair down to the floor — may fail to lock. When they do not lock, the wheelchair is not really held in place and can roll or shift while the van is moving. Braun and Q'Straint will inspect the retractors and replace any bad ones, free of charge. Owner letters were mailed in June 2026.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager Curtain Airbags Lose Air Pressure
item.description: The side curtain airbags in these vans — the long airbags that come down over the side windows — have seams that were not sealed properly. Because of that, they can lose air pressure too quickly instead of staying inflated, so they may not hold you inside the vehicle during a crash or rollover. Dealers will replace the curtain airbags as needed. This recall replaces two earlier ones, so vans already fixed before still need the new repair.

item.title: Wheelchair van restraints may not lock in Odyssey, Pacifica, Sienna
item.description: These minivans were converted by Vantage Mobility so a wheelchair can ride inside. The wheelchair is held down by belt-style restraints with retractors that are supposed to lock, much like a seat belt locks. On these vans, the retractors may fail to lock, so the wheelchair is not really tied down. If it is not secured, the chair and the person in it can roll or tip while the van is moving, braking, or turning.

item.title: Rollx Wheelchair Vans: Restraints May Not Lock Wheelchair
item.description: These are vans converted by Rollx for wheelchair use. The straps that hold a wheelchair use retractors, which work like a seat belt: they pull in slack and then lock so the chair cannot roll. On these vans, the QRT-Deluxe and QRT-Max retractors may fail to lock. If they do not lock, the wheelchair and the person in it can shift or slide while the van is moving, which raises the risk of injury. Rollx and the restraint maker will check the retractors and replace them if needed.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager side curtain airbags lose pressure
item.description: The long airbags that drop down from above the side windows on some 2025 Pacifica and Voyager minivans may have seams that were not sealed correctly. That means they can lose air pressure too quickly when they inflate, so they may not stay firm long enough to keep people from being thrown out of a side window in a crash. Dealers replace them free. Note: a newer recall, 26V189, replaces this one, and vans already fixed need the new repair too.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica wrong radio can blank backup camera
item.description: Some Pacifica minivans were built with the wrong radio, and that radio can keep the backup camera picture from appearing on the screen. Federal safety rules require a working rearview image, so these vans did not meet the standard. Without the camera view you cannot see everything behind you while reversing. Chrysler says dealers have already replaced the radio in every affected van at no charge, and owner letters were mailed in August 2025.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager backup camera may go blank
item.description: A manufacturing mistake means the backup camera picture may not show up on the dashboard screen when you shift into reverse. Instead of seeing what is behind the van, the screen may stay blank. Federal safety rules require a working rear view image, so these vans do not meet the standard. A dealer will check the camera and install a new one if it is needed, at no cost to you.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager side curtain airbags may leak
item.description: The side curtain airbags — the long airbags that drop down over the side windows — may have seams that were not sealed properly. An airbag that leaks loses air too fast and may not stay firm through a crash, so people inside are less protected from being thrown out of a window. This recall has since been replaced by a newer one, 26V189, and vehicles already repaired under it need the newer repair too.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager vans missing seat stop part
item.description: A small part called a seat limiter, which stops the seat from sliding too far forward, may have been left out of these Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager vans by the company that modified them. Without it, the seat can end up closer to the airbag than it should be. Airbags inflate very quickly and with force, so sitting too close to one raises the chance of being hurt in a crash. A dealer checks the seat and installs the limiter if it is missing.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager Side Curtain Airbags May Not Deploy
item.description: A plug that connects the side curtain airbags — the ones that drop down from above the side windows to protect your head in a side crash or rollover — was not pushed in and locked properly at the factory. If that connector is loose, those airbags may not go off when you need them. Chrysler says the fix is simply securing the connector, and dealers have already completed the repair on all affected vans.

item.title: Jeep, Ram, Chrysler backup camera may show nothing
item.description: The radio software in these vehicles can keep the backup camera picture from appearing at all. When you shift into reverse, the screen may not show what is behind you, so you cannot see a child, a person, or an object in the vehicle's path while backing up. That makes it much easier to hit something you never saw. The repair is a software update for the radio, done at the dealer or sent to the vehicle wirelessly.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager lose traction control with cruise on
item.description: Traction control is the system that quietly cuts wheel spin when a tire starts to slip — on wet roads, snow, or loose gravel. On these vans, traction control stops working whenever cruise control is switched on. That means the van could slide more easily than you expect in slippery conditions. Until the fix is done, avoid using cruise control when the road is wet, icy, or snowy. The dealer will update the software at no charge.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager windshield may not be glued properly
item.description: The windshield is glued to the body of the van, and that bond is part of the vehicle's safety structure. On these vans the glue may not have been applied correctly, so the windshield could come away from the van in a crash. If it does, people inside are less protected during the crash and can be injured. The van drives normally otherwise. The dealer will install a new windshield free of charge.

item.title: Dodge Charger and Chrysler 300 Curtain Airbags May Rupture
item.description: On certain Dodge Charger and Chrysler 300 cars, the side curtain airbags that run above the side windows were built with a defect. The metal canister that fills the bag with gas can burst instead of inflating the bag the way it should. If that happens, sharp pieces of metal can fly into the passenger area and strike the people inside. Dealers will replace both the right and left side curtain airbags at no cost to you.

item.title: Jeep, Ram and Chrysler vehicles: driver airbag may not deploy
item.description: A part in the steering column may not have been welded correctly at the factory. That part carries the electrical signal to the driver's airbag in the steering wheel. If the weld is bad, the airbag may not inflate during a crash, so the driver would not get the protection it is supposed to give. A dealer will check the part and replace it if needed at no cost to you.

item.title: Chrysler 300, Charger, Challenger parking brake may not hold
item.description: The parking brake on these cars may not have been adjusted correctly when they were built. That means the brake may not hold the car the way it should, and the car can roll away after you park it. Because of this, the vehicles also do not meet the federal safety rule for light vehicle brakes. A dealer will adjust the parking brake properly, and the work is free. Owner letters went out in late February 2024.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica plug-in hybrid battery part can cause fire
item.description: These 2023 Pacifica plug-in hybrids have a part on the 12-volt battery, called an isolator post, that may have been installed wrong. That can cause an electrical short, and the short can start a fire, either while you are driving or while the van is sitting parked. Chrysler says to park outside and away from buildings until it is repaired. A dealer will refit the part correctly at no cost.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica plug-in hybrid fuel line may leak gasoline
item.description: The fuel line on some 2023 Chrysler Pacifica plug-in hybrid minivans may be bent or squashed out of shape, and that can let gasoline leak out. Leaking fuel near anything hot or sparking can start a fire. Dealers will inspect the fuel line and install a new one if it needs it, at no cost to you. Chrysler mailed notification letters to owners at the end of August 2023.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica Hybrid may shut off while driving
item.description: In these plug-in hybrid Pacifica minivans, a wiring connector inside the transmission can short out. When that happens, the engine can shut down without warning while you are driving, and the van loses the power that moves it. You could be left coasting in traffic or on the highway. The fix is a software update that changes how the vehicle's electronics handle the problem.

item.title: Dodge Charger, Challenger, Chrysler 300 tire pressure sensors fail
item.description: These Dodge Challenger, Dodge Charger, and Chrysler 300 cars have small sensors in the wheels that watch your tire pressure. The batteries inside those sensors can die early, so a sensor stops working. Then the car cannot warn you when a tire is actually low. Worse, if the warning light is already lit because of a dead sensor battery, you may ignore it and miss a real low tire. Driving on a low tire can cause it to fail.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager wiper arm nuts may loosen
item.description: The nuts that hold the windshield wiper arms in place may not have been tightened enough at the factory. Loose nuts can let the wiper arms slip so the wipers do not sweep the glass properly, or stop moving at all. In rain or snow that leaves you with a poor view of the road. The repair is quick: a dealer tightens the wiper arm nuts at no cost to you.

item.title: Chrysler 300, Charger, Challenger tire pressure sensors quit early
item.description: These cars have sensors in the wheels that watch your tire pressure. The battery inside a sensor can die too early, so the sensor stops working. When that happens, the system will not warn you that a tire is going low. Worse, if the warning light is already on because of a dead sensor battery, it can hide a real low-tire problem. A low tire can fail while you drive. Dealers will check the sensors and replace any bad ones.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager second-row seats may not lock
item.description: The second-row seats latch onto the floor so they stay put. On these vans the latch can stick in the open position, which means the seat may look installed but is not actually locked down. A seat that is not secured can move in a crash, and it also affects the anchors used for child safety seats. A dealer will check the latch and replace the seat cushion frame if needed.

item.title: Chrysler 300, Challenger, Charger windshield may not be glued properly
item.description: When these cars were built, the glue that holds the windshield in place may not have bonded properly. The windshield looks and works normally in everyday driving, but in a crash it could separate from the car instead of staying put, which can lead to injuries. Because of this, the vehicle does not meet the federal safety rule for windshield mounting. Your dealer will remove the old sealant, put in new sealant and refit the windshield, free of charge. Letters were mailed August 31, 2021.

item.title: Jeep, Ram, Chrysler backup camera image stays on screen
item.description: The software in your 8.4-inch or 12-inch radio screen has a bug. After you back up and shift out of reverse, the picture from the backup camera can stay on the screen instead of switching back to the normal display. That means you can be driving forward while a rear-facing picture is still showing, which can pull your eyes and attention off the road ahead. The fix is a software update for the radio screen.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica Hybrid fire risk from electrical connection
item.description: A large electrical connection behind the driver's seat in these plug-in hybrid minivans can develop a bad contact. A bad contact makes heat, and that heat can start a fire, with the van running or parked and switched off. Until the final fix is ready, Chrysler says not to park these vans inside a garage or other building, or close to other vehicles, and to keep drinks, wet umbrellas and anything else that could leak out of the back seat area.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica backup camera image stays on while driving
item.description: On these minivans, a software error can leave the backup camera picture on the dashboard screen after you have shifted out of reverse and started driving forward. A video image sitting there while you drive can pull your eyes off the road and distract you, which raises the chance of a crash. It also breaks a federal safety rule covering rear visibility. Dealers will update the radio software at no charge, and the recall began January 9, 2020.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica loose battery connection may cause stalling
item.description: On Pacificas with the system that shuts the engine off at stoplights, the battery's ground connection may be loose. A loose connection can cut electrical power on and off, so you may suddenly lose power steering assist, meaning the wheel becomes much harder to turn, or the engine may stall while you are driving. A dealer will inspect the connection, clean the contact surfaces if needed, and put it back together properly and tightly.

item.title: Chrysler 300, Charger and Challenger dash warning lights may fail
item.description: The instrument cluster is the set of gauges and warning lights right in front of the steering wheel. On these cars its software can fail to light up the warnings, so a problem with one of the car's systems might never show on the dash. You could be driving with a fault and have no idea. Federal rules require those warnings to work, so these cars do not meet the standard. A dealer will update the cluster software.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica right front control arm can separate
item.description: On certain 2018 Chrysler Pacifica and Pacifica Hybrid minivans, the lower control arm on the right front wheel can come apart from the steering knuckle — the piece it bolts to at the wheel. If that connection separates, you could crash. Dealers inspect the right front knuckle and control arm for damage, replace anything that is damaged, and fit a thicker pinch bolt to hold the joint together. The work is free.

item.title: Jeep, Ram, Dodge, Chrysler engine computer may cause stalling
item.description: The computer that runs the engine has a small part inside, a voltage regulator chip, that can fail. When it does, the engine can shut off while you are driving, or the vehicle may not start at all. A stall in traffic leaves you without engine power and can put you in the path of other vehicles. Dealers will replace the whole engine computer at no charge.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica and Jeep Cherokee transmission may stop working
item.description: A part inside the automatic transmission may not have been welded properly. The transmission is what sends engine power to the wheels. If that weld breaks, the connection is lost and the vehicle simply stops moving — the engine may still be running, but the wheels get no power. Losing drive without warning, especially in traffic or at speed, raises the risk of a crash. Chrysler dealers will replace the entire transmission at no cost to you.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica axle shaft may come apart
item.description: The front halfshafts, the shafts that carry engine power to the front wheels, may have been put together incorrectly at the factory, so a shaft may not be properly locked into its joint. If it comes apart, the van can suddenly lose power to the wheels while you are driving. It can also roll away on its own even when the shifter is in Park. Dealers will replace the affected halfshaft at no cost.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica park release plug can be pulled out
item.description: On these minivans, the manual park release plug — the small cover you can pull to shift the transmission out of park by hand — can be taken off without any tool. Federal safety rules say it should not come off that easily. If someone pulls it out and the release gets used by accident, the van can slip out of park and roll away on its own, possibly hitting someone standing nearby. Dealers will install a new plug free of charge.

item.title: Chrysler, Dodge, Jeep and Ram cruise control may stick on
item.description: These vehicles have cruise control, which holds a set speed for you. A short circuit in the wiring can lock the cruise control on. If that happens, tapping the brake pedal or pressing the off button may not shut it off, and the vehicle can keep its speed or even speed up on its own. Chrysler tells owners to stop using cruise control until the free computer software update is done at a dealer.

item.title: Chrysler, Dodge, Jeep, RAM may not stay in Park
item.description: The wrong part may have been installed inside the automatic transmission. It is a rod that locks the transmission when you move the shifter into Park. If the wrong rod is in there, the transmission may not actually lock, so the vehicle can roll on its own after you think you have parked it. That could hurt someone standing nearby or cause a crash. A dealer installs the correct rod for free.
